distance runner and Club Champion; bests include marathon 2hr 46min 06sec (Poly Marathon 1952) and London - Brighton 6hr 38min 20sec (1952); in his latter 50s in 1977; born in Kensington June 2nd 1921; schoolboy at Beaufort House; Church Lads Brigade; joined Belgrave November 2nd 1938; won five mile cross country handicap October 1947; first Polytechnic Marathon 1948 in 3 hours 17 minutes 1 second; ran fourteen consecutive Poly marathons, last in 1961; 29th and first Belgrave home in the 1952 Polytechnic Marathon (Olympic trial), 2 hours 46 minutes 6 seconds, earning a Club Championship and Honours Badge; 16th in the first Road Runners Club London to Brighton run, August 27th 1952; R.R.C. 2nd class award 1954; made a Vice-President in 1972

photos.c: SUNDAY MORNING AT ARTHUR'S Some of the "gang" enjoying refreshments---and Ron Linstead's clowning---on the lawn of Lauriston Cottage. L. to R. (rear)Charlie Dabbs, Charlie Smart,Trevor Hart,Ron Mitchell,Arthur Bruce,Howard Satchell,Ron Linstead,Mel Thorpe,John Thresher. L. to R. (front)Peter Wrench,John Dear,Gordon Biscoe,Charlie Manning.

The 10,000 metre championship for the "Tom Carter" Cup. Top left: Lionel Mann leads the main bunch - Brian Gorman, Paul Roche, Leo Coy and Jamie Stevenson. Top centre: Charlie Manning attempts to hold on to Martin Best. Top right: Second-placer Colin Pearson. Bottom left: A rare appearance on the track for Stuart Masterson, here leading Keith Duckett and junior Richard Dorman. Bottom right: Steve Williams, who in his first season of track athletics has raced over all distances from 200 to 10,000 metres.
"MR. PRESIDENT 1989" DIGS IN. Leo Coy puts the final touches to planting of the Belgrave Harriers Centenary Tree watched by Carl and Barbara Lawton, Harry Porter, Chas Manning and Tom Carter.

Left: Enjoying the occasion.  Pat Mead, Tony Binda, Marianne Black, Gerry North, Alan Black, the late Laurie O'Hara, George Piddington, Charlie Henn, Ted Pallant, Chris Steer, Charlie Manning.

Sadly this was the last time that we saw Laurie O'Hara.  He died the following day while out running.
Above: Head Boy Clive Shippen, back from Botany Bay for the occasion, gives social climber Charlie Manning a few tips.

Above: Chas (18) tears into the lead on the first lap of a Club Championship 880 yards Race at Battersea Park. We are not absolutely certain of the year but it was probably 1955, one of the years when Charlie Walker, (4) at the back of the pack became Club Champion over the distance. Behind Charlie Manning can be seen a youthful Jim Heathfield. Can anyone put names to the other faces in the picture?

Above: It's first day of May 1954 and the smiling band above are 5 to 6 miles into the Surrey 20 miles Road Race Championship held at Mitcham. Chas. (12) was 23rd gaining a Surrey County Standard with a time of 2:14:10. Len Adams (16) and John Baker (15) can also be identified.

Above: Fortythree years later and the old codger's still on the move! 24th August 1997 and Chas. (174) lines up for the Veterans A.C. 1500 metres Championship at Kingsmeadow. His time was ... well we won't go into that ... but is this a good case for euthanasia? Maybe we should pay him not to wear our club kit! Seriously though, 1,500 metres is now way over his best distance because in 1998 Chas became the Surrey County M70 Champion over 100 metres!

Third from the left, standing back, is Dave McMullen and wearing 62 is 5,000 metre ace from the '50s and current UK Athletics Council Member - Chris Chataway.
'Cover boy' for th's issue is none other than our President for 1973/1974 Charlie Manning.

photos.c:
Above: Fortythree years later and the old codger's still on the move! 24th August 1997 and Chas. (174) lines up for the Veterans A.C. 1500 metres Championship at Kingsmeadow. His time was ... well we won't go into that ... but is this a good case for euthanasia? Maybe we should pay him not to wear our club kit! Seriously though, 1,500 metres is now way over his best distance because in 1998 Chas became the Surrey County M70 Champion over 100 metres!

Third from the left, standing back, is Dave McMullen and wearing 62 is 5,000 metre ace from the '50s and current UK Athletics Council Member - Chris Chataway.

photos.c: BOTTOM RIGHT: Don Maclean crosses the line just 65 secs. behind T.V.H.

No, this is not Don Maclean the cross-country runner being helped from the finishing line of the Orion 15 race, but Don Maclean the would-be rescuer after his brave effort to save a girl from the icy waters of the Thames on a cold February day.
Don trails Mal Robinson and Pat Newall at the half distance in the 1961 Belgrave mile championship. Don was beaten on the tape by John Davies, with Newall 3rd and Robinson 4th.

Ron Linstead's camera portrays the agony of the effort (Clive Shippen) and the pleasure of the reward (Don Maclean). There is no truth in the story that Don renews his strength by drinking Courage -- he drinks it simply because £100 was tucked in his shoes!

If you think this is a picture of a marathon runner coming to the end of a marathon, you are quite right. It is our new marathon record holder Lionel Mann, obviously not superstitious.

The 5¾-miles championship field, still hunched after one mile. Front row: Pat O'Connor (12), Tony Fairclough (21), Peter Carton (19), Trevor Hart (23), and Lionel Mann (9). The three framed heads look like those of Chris Steer, John Thresher and Dereck Fernee.

MANN SUPREME - CHEF RUNS OFF WITH AWARD. Marathon champion Lionel Mann, the Galloping Cordon Bleu, being presented with the "Mitchell Trophy" for the first Belgrave Harrier home in the "Poly Marathon". The "Mitchell Trophy"is being awarded by the donor of this magnificent shield, Bert Mitchell of 32, Manor Road, Deal. Bert was formerly a fierce competitor and still remains a staunch Belgrave Harrier.
The ceremony was conducted at the 21st Annual 20 Mile Road Race at Wimbledon where Lionel also ran a blistering 1hr 54 minutes for the course.
Bottom right: 'A' team regular - Lionel Mann.
Wild man of the woods? Lionel Mann on his way to second place in the Club 10 miles cross country championship.

Lionel Mann is sent on his way by Pat O'Connor in the Belgrave Relay

The 10,000 metre championship for the "Tom Carter" Cup. Top left: Lionel Mann leads the main bunch - Brian Gorman, Paul Roche, Leo Coy and Jamie Stevenson. Top centre: Charlie Manning attempts to hold on to Martin Best. Top right: Second-placer Colin Pearson. Bottom left: A rare appearance on the track for Stuart Masterson, here leading Keith Duckett and junior Richard Dorman. Bottom right: Steve Williams, who in his first season of track athletics has raced over all distances from 200 to 10,000 metres.
Front Cover: The harrier season is over but Lionel Mann shows signs of picking up some of his old form in good time for a season on the roads.
Back Page: Two of Belgrave's long serving stalwarts. Laurie O'Hara hands over to Lionel Mann during the 100 x 1 mile relay.

Lionel leads Bob Smith, Dick Piotrowski, and Adrian Major during the Belgrave 7½ miles Cross Country Championship of 1968 but all four had to give way to Tony Fairclough (1st), Laurie O'Hara (2nd) and Pat O'Connor (3rd) by the finish. The field was 36 strong.

Above: Darrin Morris explains some of the finer points of the throwing events to Paul Edwards during the reception at the British Ambassador's residence in Budapest!

BELS IN BUDAPEST

Top (left to right): Phil Spivey watches Racing Club's Yuri Sedykh put the competition beyond anyone else's reach while preparing for his own throw. While eventual 'chase winner Lambruschini lopes along at the back, Justin Chaston is in the thick of the action. Discus thrower Darrin Morris placed 5th. A "home team" decision may have cost shot-putter Paul Edwards 2nd place.
Bottom: Neil Owen surges through the high hurdles field after his blocks slipped. Derek Browne had five no jumps before a superb last effort overtook a class field including one time Olympic Champion Khristo Markhov. John Regis relaxes in the shade before a scintillating 10.15 100m - as a non-scorer! Spearman Niigel Bevan fires a 3rd-placing 71.78.

Youth Gavin Mason prepares to strike in the Tonbridge 1500 metres. Gavin has had a great season over events ranging from 200 to 1500 metres. In the Surrey Schools he ran to 3rd place in the 800 metres with 1:58.0.
Above: Ranked at number 2 under 17 in the country over 800 metres, Gavin Mason prepares for a leg in a McDonalds YA League 4x400m.

Above: It's winter again. The Under 17s are missing Matt Hillier in the County Champs but have a scoring four right at the front. Left to right are Gavin Mason (9), Toby Earle (1), Scott Walsh, and Adam Jones (6)

Right: Gavin Mason pauses between reps while Clive Shippen gets busy with the camera. When Gavin clocked 48.89 to place 7th in the British League 'A' 400 metres on 2nd July he further complicated a little statistical anomaly. John Gladwin's Under 20 Club Record set in 1989 is a hand timed 48.9, but going back to 1977 Dave Mote also ran 48.9 as a Junior for Surrey AC. Surrey amalgamated with Belgrave in 1982 and therefore Dave had a 50% (and little known) claim on that record.

Above: A long but superb season has come from 400 metre man Robert Milner. As early as April 18th he clocked 40.0 for a 300 at Tooting and then, as the summer wore, on he chipped away at his one lap times with his best of 53.6 coming in June at Kingsmeadow. He was "Man of the Match at Tonbridge, placed 3rd in the South of England Boys' Champs in 53.92, won the Inter-County match at Battersea and placed 2nd in the Southern Inter-Counties at Hayes in late August with 53.7.

photos.c: 1. One of the most glorious sights in athletics is the start of the Senior Men's National Cross Country Championships. Half a mile into the 2000 race at Stowe School, Buckinghhamshire, and the field is led by Belgrave's Paul Evans with Paul Freary just behind him and to the right. On the left, behind 2516 is Kevin Nash and next but one above 2321 is Rob McHarg. On the right, behind the orange vested .24 is Jason Lobo, making a more conservative start, with Lee Hurst next but one on the left of .24. In the centre, just behind and to the right of the Blackheath vest is Alaster Stewart and next on the right, with only his claret bandana showing is Charles Herrington. That's eight in the top 100 and they spent the next half mile gaining even more forward positions. You might have to take the Editor's word for this one: on the skyline just to the left of the tree can be seen Phil Carstairs' thinning thatch. Will Cockerell has also been picked out in this vicinity by one viewer - but blowed if we can find him now!

The traditional team photo before the start of the first Surrey League Race. Back row - Bruce Barton, Geremew Wolde, Rex Bale, Mike Webb, Don Anderson, Gerry Adams, Darryl Ochse, Alasdair McLean Foreman, Roger Alsop, Adam Cowmeadow, Tony Barden, Kevin Quinn, Pete Gilbey, Harry Corbett, Erwenn Lemenager, Rob Harding, Andy Brown, Ted Pallant. Front row: Rob McHarg, Steve Clarke, Will Cockerell, Eric Hall (President), Junior Galley, Jamie Kirton, Elvis Rimdap, Roy Collier, Aldis Ulrych.

Right: An hour before "National" race time. Bill Laws and John Jeffery have driven back to Milton Keynes to pick up Paul Evans whose car has broken down, leaving the rest of the team to pose for the pre-race photo. Back row: Eric Hall (President), Don Anderson, Paul Coughlan, Alan Mead, Alaster Stewart, Paul Freary, Jason Lobo, Kevin Nash, Phil Carstairs, Rob Harding. Front: Darryl Ochse, Will Cockerell, Charles Herrington, Lee Hurst, Rob McHarg.

Above: Irish eyes were not the only ones smiling when the the Belgrave team collected their prizes in Wallace Park. Rob McHarg, Paul Freary, Alaster Stewart, Yacin Yusuf (crouching), Jason Lobo and Spencer Barden enjoy being Irish Road Relay Champions.

photos.c: Mark Miles - numero uno! Two 5 kms and two wins in Gold Cup competition.
Left: Mark Miles took up the pace for most of the 'A' 1500m at Copthall before getting jumped by the pack over the last 300 metres.
Below: Ignoring the pouring rain at the end of the race. Lee Hurst, Paul Freary, Spencer Barden, Jason Lobo, Paul Evans and Mark Miles.

Belgrave's Winning AAA 12-Stage Team at Sutton Park. Back row: Andy Graffin, Spencer Barden, Paul Freary, Stephen Sharp, Alaster Stewart, David Anderson, Allen Graffin, Paul Evans. Front row: Lee Hurst, Mark Miles, Alan Mead (team manager), Richard Ward, Charles Herrington.

Above (1): Belgrave's men retained the AAA 6-Stage Road Relay Championship at Sutton Park in October 2002. Mark Miles, Richard Ward, Spencer Barden, Stephen Sharp, Allen Graffin and David Anderson celebrate keeping hold of the trophy for another year. This is the hardest team title to win - can they make it three in a row in October 2003?
Bottom left: Mark Miles took the Belgrave lead to over two minutes on stage 5.

Above: The start of the inaugural AAA 5 km Road Championship, held in conjunction with the Horwich Carnival race.  From left to right Peter Riley (107 Leigh H), Rob Whalley (90 Bristol & West AC), Andi Jones (51 Salford), David Anderson (88 Belgrave H) with Mark Miles on his left, behind Ian Mitchell (114 Tipton), the eventual winner Wilf Taragon (85 Birchfield), Mark Tucker (126 Australia), Birhan Dagne (217 Belgrave H) is on the right.  Mark Miles placed second with the fastest time run by a Briton in Britain this year – 13:58 – and took the AAA Championship.
Mark Miles staged a terrific finish in the AAA 5k to all but catch Wilf Taragon (Birchfield/Kenya)

Above: The AAA 5k Road Race was again held in Horwich. It was only the second time the Championship has been held and the Bels have medalled on each occasion – silver in 2005 and now gold in 2006. Individual AAA Champion was Chris Davies of Telford (in the red and yellow), second was Peter Riley of Leigh (white vest with green diagonal) and third was our own Mark Miles (177). Simon Jones (not pictured) and Richard Ward (181) made up the Belgrave team. The Open race was won by Birchfield, running three Africans, but they were not eligible for the AAA race.

Above: Maximum points in the 5000 metres.  At the halfway point Mark Miles was closely shadowed by John Nysaginia (Birchfield) and our own Stephen Sharp but by the end of the race the gap was 11 seconds with Stephen heading the B race by 20 seconds.

NATIONAL 6-STAGE ROAD RELAY CHAMPIONS – 2007
Yes, we’ve brought you pictures like this before – but while our lads are able to notch up such great victories, we’ll have no hesitation in bringing you further such images. Left to right: James Kelly (stage 2), Phil Wicks (6), Stephen Sharp (1), Mark Miles (5), Jonathan Blackledge (3) and Simon Jones (4)

NATIONAL CROSS COUNTRY RELAY CHAMPIONS – 2007
A third National title of the Autumn season came Belgrave’s way at the end of a riveting race at Berry Hill Park, Mansfield. It was only the second time in our history that we’ve managed to pull this one off. Left to right: Mark Pollard (stage 2), Stephen Sharp (1), Phil Wicks (4), Mark Miles (3).

photos.c: Above: The start of the Eastleigh 10k on March 19th.  The race included the CAU Inter-Counties Championship and Belgravians were racing in some unfamiliar vests.  In the red vest with white/red shorts towards the left is the eventual race winner Angus Maclean (Team Southampton). 31 is Richard Ward (Belgrave/Surrey), 32 Phil Wicks (Belgrave/Surrey), between and just behind  these latter two is Tim Watson in a white/green vest (Belgrave/Hampshire).  To the right of Phil is Hassan Raidi (Belgrave/Surrey), Jonathan Blackledge (Belgrave), and 15 Jermain Mays (Kent AC/Kent).
